title: Spectral Reduction and Logarithmic Observation Response in a Discrete Coexact Model
abstract: We study a finite counting-norm vector-field model on an even three-dimensional torus with checkerboard source weights and original componentwise rectangular means. On the actual image of the forward curl adjoint we derive the complete two-polarization Fourier spectrum, including the absent zero mode and exceptional pair. For H=cn^2 and a=c/48 the whole subtarget space has dimension n-2 per channel. The original high modes realize every coexact observation; an explicit polynomial lift and exact shifted cancellation-cost criterion follow with dependent rows. For permutation singleton cuts we prove finite logarithmic upper and lower response bounds and show that growth persists on useful positive-weight low data. These exclude two uniform response estimates without deciding optimized cancellation. A logarithmic lower bound for invisible coexact fields follows. The arguments are finite and analytical. Classical Green logarithms are credited; priority of the model-specific comparisons is unestablished. No continuum or physical Yang-Mills gap is claimed.
